items.title: Deepmind founder Hassabis shortens AGI timeline from five to two to three years
items.summary: Demis Hassabis keeps moving up his AGI timeline. The Nobel laureate and former Google Deepmind CEO now expects artificial general intelligence within two to three years, down from three to five years earlier this year. The article Deepmind founder Hassabis shortens AGI timeline from five to two to three years appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Inception's Mercury 3 diffusion model claims to beat GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at a fraction of the wait
items.summary: Inception says Mercury 3 is the most capable diffusion language model released so far. The company claims it runs four to eight times faster than GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 and beats both in eight of 12 benchmarks. There are no independent tests yet. items.title: China protests the US Deepseek ban while blocking ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini at home
items.summary: The US has banned Deepseek from its government systems, and China is protesting sharply and demanding the ban be lifted. Yet Beijing itself blocks ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini across its entire market. China's outrage isn't very credible, but it should be taken seriously as a political signal of possible retaliation. The article China protests the US Deepseek ban while blocking ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini at home appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: OpenAI can't yet explain why its coding agents switch off misalignment monitoring
items.summary: Two internal OpenAI coding agents switched off safety monitoring on their own, even after weighing whether to keep the safeguards in place. When asked about it, GPT-6 Astra denied removing the monitoring. OpenAI calls this a recurring pattern and doesn't yet have a satisfying explanation for the behavior. The article OpenAI can't yet explain why its coding agents switch off misalignment monitoring appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Claude Science tackles deadly scorpion stings by designing protein binders from scratch
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude independently designed protein binders targeting deadly scorpion neurotoxins. Out of more than 318,000 designs, 211 were tested in the lab. Seventeen met the criteria, and the two strongest bind extremely tightly to Cn2, a toxin from a Mexican scorpion. Whether they actually work as antivenom remains an open question. items.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to build AI agents that speed up drug development
items.summary: OpenAI is acquiring startup Orchestra Bio and plans to merge it with its life sciences AI platform Rosalind. The goal is to build AI agents that help pharma teams coordinate drug development, from tracking trials to spotting problems. Developing a new drug in the US takes ten to 15 years on average. items.title: Elevenlabs releases two new speech-to-speech models designed for real-time AI conversations
items.summary: Elevenlabs' new Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models combine speed and accuracy. The v1 Max variant scores 98.8 percent on the Big Bench Audio benchmark with a 0.57-second response time. Elevenlabs says no model on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard is both faster and more accurate. The article Elevenlabs releases two new speech-to-speech models designed for real-time AI conversations appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Deepseek open-sources the inference engine that powers its fastest and cheapest AI model
items.summary: Deepseek is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its fast V4.1-Flash model. The vLLM-based system cuts compute costs and energy use when running AI models. The release adds more pricing pressure on Western providers like OpenAI and Anthropic.
